title: Find Eventual Safe States
summary: List the nodes of a directed graph from which every walk is guaranteed to stop at a dead end.

tests.explain: 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 ends at 3, which has no outgoing edges, so 0 to 3 are safe. 4 and 5 point at each other forever. 6 has an edge into that loop, so it is unsafe.
0 and 1 form a loop. 2 can only go to 3, a terminal node, so 2 and 3 are safe.
Node 0 has an edge to itself, so a walk from it never has to stop: it isn't safe.

hints: A node is unsafe exactly when some path from it reaches a cycle. Nodes with no outgoing edges are safe by definition.
Work backwards from the dead ends: reverse every edge and run Kahn's algorithm on out-degrees. A node whose outgoing edges all lead to safe nodes becomes safe itself.
Alternatively, DFS with three colours: a node is safe if its search finishes without meeting a node that is still on the current path. Either way, return the safe nodes in increasing order.

complexity.time: O(V + E): each node is queued once and each edge is reversed and used once
complexity.space: O(V + E): the reversed graph, the out-degrees and the queue
